finalText:
Migration finished.

## What changed

12 files were still on `db.query`, 36 call sites total — 3 in each file (get-by-id, list, update):

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the shape the earlier passes established in the already-migrated siblings. I did this with a bracket-aware codemod rather than a regex, because the update sites pass `[...keys.map((k) => patch[k]), id]` — the nested `patch[k]` breaks naive `\[...\]` matching.

## Two things I deliberately did not change

**`cache.query()` is not the same API.** `lib/cache.js` exposes a `query` that takes a cache key, not SQL — the shared name is a coincidence, and `lib/cache.js:3` says so explicitly. It appears in 6 of the files I touched (e.g. `session.js:18`), sitting two lines from a real `db.query`. Left as-is; the codemod asserted on the receiver rather than pattern-matching `.query(`.

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` still has 2 `db.query` calls**, and I left them. The file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on every upgrade, with local edits silently lost. Migrating it would look done but silently revert on the next vendor bump. Worth flagging: since `lib/db.js:6` notes the driver's next major *drops* `query`, this is a real upgrade blocker that needs handling upstream — bump legacy-orm to a version using the new form, or wrap the adapter. That's a call for you, not something to bury in this sweep. Say the word if you want the wrapper.

## Verification

No test suite, package.json, or git in this repo, so I wrote a throwaway harness against the fact that `lib/db.js` records the `form` of every call. It required all 75 package modules, invoked all 250 exported functions, and captured 325 db calls: **325 `execute`, 0 `query`**, 0 malformed payloads (every one carries a non-empty `sql` string and an array `params`), no load or call errors. Both scratch scripts lived outside the repo and are deleted.

Caveat on what that proves: it confirms every call site now reaches `execute` with a well-formed payload, since `lib/db.js` is a stub that just records and returns `[]`. It does not exercise a real driver, so nothing here validates the SQL itself against a database.
